map: Stationarity gives (B+lambda I)s_*=-g. At s_*=0 the second-order condition gives B positive semidefinite.
For nonzero s_*, Eq.(3.3) gives nonnegative quadratic form of B+lambda I on vectors orthogonal to s_*.
For other directions, compare s_* to the second intersection of that line with the sphere of radius ||s_*||. Eqs.(3.5)–(3.10) yield nonnegativity in those directions, completing necessity.

proofs.full_local_argument: Let r=||s_*|| and A=B+sigma r I. The function ||s||^3 is C^2, with gradient 3||s||s and Hessian zero at 0; at s!=0 its Hessian is 3||s||I+3ss^T/||s||. Thus any global minimizer satisfies g+A s_*=0. If r=0, second-order necessity gives B=A positive semidefinite. If r>0, second-order necessity gives w^T[A+(sigma/r)s_*s_*^T]w>=0 for every w. For w orthogonal to s_* this gives w^TAw>=0. For w with w^Ts_*!=0, put t=-2(w^Ts_*)/||w||^2, so t!=0 and u=s_*+tw satisfies ||u||=r. By symmetry of B and stationarity, m(u)-m(s_*)=(1/2)(u-s_*)^TB(u-s_*)-sigma r s_*^T(u-s_*). Equal radii imply 2s_*^T(u-s_*)+||u-s_*||^2=0, so the difference equals (t^2/2)w^TAw. Global minimality makes this nonnegative, hence w^TAw>=0. All directions have now been covered and A is positive semidefinite. Conversely suppose g=-A s_* and A is positive semidefinite. For arbitrary u let q=||u|| and h=u-s_*. Expanding the quadratic and substituting stationarity yields m(u)-m(s_*)=(1/2)h^TAh+sigma[(q^3-r^3)/3-r(q^2-r^2)/2]=(1/2)h^TAh+(sigma/6)(q-r)^2(2q+r)>=0. This holds also for r=0, proving global minimality. If A is positive definite and u!=s_*, the first term is strictly positive, proving uniqueness. All steps apply for any g, including zero, and permit singular A.

assumptions: B is a real symmetric d-by-d matrix.
sigma>0; c is real and g belongs to R^d.
No positive-definiteness or invertibility assumption on B or A is imposed for the equivalence.
statement.conclusion: s_* is a global minimizer of m over all R^d if and only if A s_*=-g and A is positive semidefinite, with lambda=sigma||s_*||. If these conditions hold and A is positive definite, s_* is the unique global minimizer.
statement.objects_and_definitions: On R^d with Euclidean norm, let m(s)=c+g^T s+(1/2)s^T B s+(sigma/3)||s||^3. For a candidate s_* define r=||s_*||, lambda=sigma r and A=B+lambda I_d.
statement.parameter_domains: d is an integer >=1; c in R; g in R^d; B=B^T in R^{dxd}; sigma in (0,infinity).
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible d,c,g,B,sigma and every s_* in R^d, the stated equivalence holds deterministically. The local argument includes g=0 and s_*=0; source context Eq.(2.40) otherwise uses a nonzero-gradient convention.

title: Global optimality characterization for a cubic-regularized quadratic
